# Job Chapter 19 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 422v–423r

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Then Job answered and said:

**2** "How long will you torment me and crush me with words? **3** These ten times you have humiliated me; are you not ashamed to wrong me?

**4** Even if it is true that I have erred, my error remains with me. **5** If indeed you exalt yourselves against me and argue my disgrace against me,

**6** know then that God has wronged me, and closed his net around me.

**7** Behold, I cry out, 'Violence!' but I am not answered; I call for help, but there is no justice.

**8** He has walled up my way so that I cannot pass, and he has set darkness upon my paths. **9** He has stripped my glory from me and taken the crown from my head.

**10** He breaks me down on every side, and I am gone; he has uprooted my hope like a tree. **11** He has kindled his wrath against me and counts me as his enemy.

**12** His troops come on together; they have raised their siege ramp against me and encamp around my tent.

**13** He has put my brothers far from me, and those who knew me are wholly estranged from me. **14** My relatives have failed me, and my close friends have forgotten me. **15** The guests in my house and my maidservants count me as a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their eyes. **16** I call to my servant, but he gives me no answer; I must plead with him with my own mouth.

**17** My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to the children of my own family. **18** Even young boys despise me; when I rise, they talk against me. **19** All my closest friends abhor me, and those I loved have turned against me.

**20** My bones cling to my skin and to my flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

**21** Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, O you my friends, for the hand of God has struck me!

**22** Why do you, like God, pursue me? Why are you not satisfied with my flesh?

**23** Oh that my words were written down! Oh that they were inscribed in a book! **24** Oh that with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!

**25** For I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last he will stand upon the earth.

**26** And after my skin has been thus destroyed, yet from my flesh I shall see God, **27** whom I shall see for myself, and my eyes shall behold, and not another. My heart faints within me!

**28** If you say, 'How we will pursue him!' and, 'The root of the matter is found in him,' **29** be afraid of the sword yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Job 19 is the emotional and theological climax of the second cycle and arguably of the entire book. The structure moves from accusation against the friends (vv.2-6), through a description of God's assault (vv.7-12), into the devastating catalogue of abandonment (vv.13-19), to the desperate plea for pity (vv.21-22), and finally erupts into the great confession (vv.25-27). The progression is essential: the Redeemer declaration does not arise from theological calm but from total isolation. Job has been abandoned by everyone — brothers, friends, servants, wife, children, neighbors — and it is from this abyss that he cries out for a vindicator. The *go'el* of v.25 represents the deepest paradox of the book: Job appeals to God against God. The one who has wronged him (v.6) is the same one who will vindicate him (v.25). Verses 25-27, whatever their precise meaning, represent the furthest point to which faith under suffering can reach in the Old Testament.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.6 — "put me in the wrong" vs. "wronged me"
- **EMET:** "God has-wronged-me [ivvetani]"
- **LOGOS:** "God has put me in the wrong"
- **PNEUMA:** "it is God who has wronged me"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "God has wronged me" — the Hebrew *ivvetani* (from *avath*, to twist/distort/wrong) is a direct accusation of injustice against God. LOGOS's "put me in the wrong" softens the accusation, implying God declared Job guilty rather than that God himself committed wrong. The bolder reading is more faithful to the Hebrew.

### V.25 — "upon the earth" vs. "upon the dust"
- **EMET:** "upon dust [al afar] he-will-stand"
- **LOGOS:** "upon the earth"
- **PNEUMA:** "upon the earth"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "upon the earth" — Hebrew *afar* literally means "dust," but here it refers to the earth/ground where the *go'el* will take his stand. "Earth" is clearer in English; "dust" could wrongly suggest the grave or the afterlife.

### V.26 — "from my flesh" — embodied or disembodied vision?
- **EMET:** "from-my-flesh I-will-see God" (notes ambiguity)
- **LOGOS:** "yet from my flesh I shall see God"
- **PNEUMA:** "from within my body I will see God"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "yet from my flesh I shall see God" — preserves the ambiguity of the Hebrew preposition *min* ("from"), which can mean "from within" or "apart from." PNEUMA's "from within my body" resolves the ambiguity in favor of embodied vision. The text should remain open, as the Hebrew is.

### V.27 — "My heart faints" vs. "My kidneys are consumed"
- **EMET:** "My-kidneys are-consumed in-my-bosom"
- **LOGOS:** "My heart faints within me"
- **PNEUMA:** "My heart aches with longing for that day"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "My heart faints within me" — the Hebrew *kilyotai kalu becheqi* literally says "my kidneys are consumed in my bosom," expressing overwhelming desire. "Heart faints" is the functional English equivalent. PNEUMA's "aches with longing for that day" adds interpretive content ("that day") not in the text.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
